A1.justification: Both PDFs describe NeuroTree and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Corresponding methods, experiments, and proofs can be matched despite substantial revisions and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments, component ablations, brain-age predictions, and functional-connectivity analyses, including Tables I and III and Figures 3–7.

after.justification: v3 reports original classification and age-prediction results in Tables 1–2, alongside connectivity analyses and additional parameter and tree-structure ablations.

M1.justification: The specified FC-processing pipeline changes substantially: v1 Section IV-B uses multi-head attention, whereas v3 Section 4.3 computes mean absolute FC and maps it through an MLP. Contrastive similarity changes from FC time courses to latent vectors, which also replace averaged FC in node scoring. Age modulation and zero-order path connectivity are revised; the k-hop ODE and MST framework remains.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Cannabis and COBRE populations, Stanford 90-ROI and Harvard-Oxford 118-ROI parcellations, and disease-classification and age-prediction tasks. Added analyses use these retained datasets; revised functional-network grouping does not introduce new data coverage.

E2.justification: Table I and Table 1 evaluate the same nine external comparators: Pearson GCN, k-NN GCN, GAT, BrainGNN, BrainUSL, BrainGSL, MixHop, GPC-GCN, and PathNN. Additional related-work citations do not become evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Reported settings change from rho=0.1 to 0.5; v1's fixed lambda=0.5 is replaced by a reported range and new lambda/Gamma performance sweeps. The regional analysis also changes its displayed grouping, incorporating SUB while dropping the separate LIM/VAN categories shown previously. Five-fold classification and its metrics remain. Healthy-control-only age training is newly specified, but v1 does not establish whether that split changed.

E4.justification: v3 adds classification sensitivity to lambda and Gamma (Appendix H/Figure 8), qualitative effects of removing age and CMFC on tree structure (Appendix K/Figure 11), and healthy-versus-disorder age-gap analysis (Figure 5). Existing classification ablations, spectral convergence, and alpha sensitivity are retained or revised; relocating the alpha analysis is not an addition.

E5.justification: Appendix L.1 newly reports preprocessing quality-control statistics: a motion-group t-test with p=0.86 and a motion–accuracy association with p=0.475, within the source-linked preprocessing description. Existing ± summaries and FC plots' SEM/significance conventions remain. No increased run count or new seed protocol is documented.

E6.justification: Table I to Table 1 changes reported NeuroTree Cannabis AUC from 0.77 to 0.80 and accuracy from 0.75 to 0.73; COBRE accuracy changes from 0.69 to 0.65. Table III's age results are replaced, its overall rows disappear, and youngest-COBRE correlation is omitted. Regional findings and agewise FC values/significance also change, alongside new ablation results. Changed methods/settings prevent interpreting these as controlled performance gains.

T1.justification: The original theoretical arguments and proofs are retained as Appendices A–D, without substantive new proofs. Limited formal definitions change: zero-order path connectivity changes from direct FC to the sum F(vi)+F(vj), and the age-modulation and connectivity-score formulas are revised. Renaming existing statements as numbered definitions or theorems is presentation only.

C1.justification: The demographic-aware ODE/tree framework, two-dataset state-of-the-art claim, and brain-age interpretation remain central. The abstract changes the claimed FC-enhancement mechanism from attention to CMFC, and the conclusion changes its highlighted network findings from DMN/FPN/VAN to DMN/FPN/VN. These are localized revisions to retained contributions.

C2.justification: v1 interprets faster cannabis spectral decay as stronger connectivity; v3 explains it through localized interactions versus preserved long-range dependencies (Appendix I). The age discussion shifts from high prediction correlations and similar disorder effects to healthy-reference age gaps, age underprediction, and greater addiction impact. Regional developmental interpretations are substantially rewritten in Appendix J, and physiological brain age is explicitly described as unobservable.

D1.justification: v3 newly documents batch size 16, 100 epochs, learning rate 0.001, hardware/software versions, detailed cannabis preprocessing, and ROI-to-network mappings. It also specifies healthy-control training for age prediction and adds repository/checkpoint information. These are substantial disclosures, not evidence that every setting changed. Availability statements conflict: the abstract says code/data are available, while the reproducibility section promises a future release.

R1.justification: v1's substantial high-order/hierarchical-GCN review, including MFGCN, HWGCN, and HFBN-GCN, is removed. v3 emphasizes neural ODE literature, adds BrainODE, and expands schizophrenia–substance-use comorbidity and brain-aging positioning in Appendix G. This changes the research context beyond citation-style conversion.

P1.justification: The abstract, related work, age-prediction section, and discussion are extensively rewritten. The architecture overview moves before the preliminaries, methodological material is reorganized, ablations enter the experiments section, and experimental details and several analyses move into expanded appendices. This is substantial narrative restructuring.

P2.justification: The framework, path-aggregation, and brain-tree figures are revised, and the age-network heatmaps are replaced. New age-gap, parameter-sensitivity, convergence-interpretation, and structural-ablation figures accompany new settings, environment, and atlas tables. Existing alpha plots and demographics are relocated, while the document changes from journal formatting to ICML formatting with single-column appendices.

improvement.justification: New training, preprocessing, environment, and atlas disclosures make v3 easier to assess and reproduce; targeted parameter and tree-structure ablations strengthen its supporting evidence. These gains are tempered by reporting inconsistencies: the conclusion retains attention-based wording after the method revision, and Table 1 reports positive Cannabis recall improvement despite PathNN's 0.83 exceeding NeuroTree's 0.74. The net improvement is limited, and revised scores under changed settings do not establish a controlled performance gain.
